title: A borehole and hand pump for forty households in Karaba
story: The nearest working water point is an hour's walk each way and it runs dry from March. Forty households in Karaba share it, and the walk falls on the girls in the family, which is why half of them stop attending school in the dry season. We are raising 14,000 USD for a borehole, a hand pump and a concrete apron, drilled by a contractor who has sunk four wells in the district. When the work is signed off the water point passes to a village committee of six, three of them women, elected before the drilling starts.
reviewerNote: Approved, and this one went to our advisor before I recorded anything. Two questions were live and they are not the same question: whether a shared water point falls inside the fi sabilillah heading under our policy, and who owns the asset once it is finished, which is where the difference between recognised positions actually bites on a project campaign. I asked the organizer and was told the completed water point passes to an elected village committee, and their constitution was sent through. Separately the forty households were evidenced as below the threshold our policy uses, and that is the basis I recorded the approval on. The advisor answered the scoped question I put, which was whether our own policy covers a project of this shape, and answered that it does with the ownership transfer documented. I am not recording a view on the wider disagreement and I have left the fi sabilillah line unresolved in the file deliberately, so the next reviewer sees the route rather than a conclusion I did not reach.
